drug_class: Complement inhibitor (a type of biologic/monoclonal antibody)
purpose: Ravulizumab-Cwvz is used to treat certain rare blood and kidney diseases, including paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS), and certain forms of a nerve-muscle disease called neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) and myasthenia gravis. It helps prevent your immune system from accidentally destroying your own blood cells or damaging your organs. This medicine can help reduce symptoms and prevent serious complications from these conditions.
how_it_works: Your immune system has a part called the complement system, which normally helps fight infections. In some people, this system goes haywire and starts attacking the body's own healthy cells. Ravulizumab works by blocking a specific protein in this system called C5, which stops the chain reaction that leads to cell destruction. Think of it like turning off a faulty switch so your immune system stops harming your own body.
common_side_effects: Headache, upper respiratory infections (like a cold), nausea, diarrhea, back pain, and dizziness are among the most common side effects. Some people may also notice injection or infusion site reactions. Most side effects are mild, but let your doctor or pharmacist know if anything feels bothersome.
warnings: The most serious risk is a life-threatening infection called meningococcal disease (a type of bacterial meningitis). Because of this, you must be vaccinated against meningococcal bacteria at least 2 weeks before starting this medication. You will carry a safety card — always have it with you. Seek emergency care right away if you develop sudden severe headache, stiff neck, fever, sensitivity to light, confusion, or a rash. Do not stop this medication without talking to your doctor, as stopping can cause your condition to suddenly get much worse.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an IV infusion (through a vein) in a clinic or hospital, usually once every 8 weeks after a starting loading dose. The exact dose and schedule depend on your weight and the condition being treated. Your healthcare team will determine the right plan for you and monitor you at each visit.
